evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif directed that Rs50,000 per flood-affected family be provided within three days and asked for transparent transfer through BISP supervision.
evidence.title: PM directs to provide cash assistance worth Rs50,000 per family to flood-affectees
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif directed that Rs50,000 per flood-affected family be provided within three days and asked for transparent transfer through BISP supervision.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official broadcaster report of a dated PM instruction with a concrete amount and timing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct PM instruction, so this is strong ruler attribution for crisis response.
contrary_evidence: The report is official and does not independently verify delivery quality or targeting accuracy.

evidence.claim: Among the flood-affected were at least 650,000 pregnant women and girls, many of whom lacked access to the healthcare facilities and support needed for safe delivery.
evidence.title: Flood-Affected Women in Pakistan Need Urgent Help
evidence.excerpt: Among the flood-affected were at least 650,000 pregnant women and girls, many of whom lacked access to the healthcare facilities and support needed for safe delivery.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent rights analysis with concrete humanitarian figures and explicit protection concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is not Sharif-caused harm, but it is a direct test of the government's protection and relief response to a major domestic crisis.
contrary_evidence: The article focuses on urgent need, not on whether government relief ultimately reached everyone adequately.

evidence.claim: Sharif said flood relief assistance under BISP would rise from Rs28 billion to Rs70 billion and each affected family would receive Rs25,000.
evidence.title: PM announces to increase BISP flood relief aid to Rs70b
evidence.excerpt: Sharif said flood relief assistance under BISP would rise from Rs28 billion to Rs70 billion and each affected family would receive Rs25,000.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PM announcement carried by the state broadcaster.
contrary_evidence: Emergency cash relief is necessary but temporary.
It does not prove durable income recovery or structural reform.

evidence.claim: UN Women distributed relief items and cash grants to vulnerable women and planned women’s centres and GBV-response services for flood-affected areas.
evidence.title: UN Women puts women and girls at the heart of flood response in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: UN Women distributed relief items and cash grants to vulnerable women and planned women’s centres and GBV-response services for flood-affected areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN reporting with specific interventions for vulnerable groups and women.
evidence.period_fit: September 2022, directly within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to the government’s disaster-response environment rather than uniquely to Sharif.
contrary_evidence: This is relief rather than long-run prosperity.
It shows crisis mitigation more than structural reform.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved $258 million for the National Health Support Program to strengthen primary health care and accelerate universal health coverage in Pakistan, with emphasis on children and women during pregnancy and childbirth.
evidence.title: World Bank Supports Primary Healthcare and Universal Coverage to Strengthen Human Capital in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved $258 million for the National Health Support Program to strengthen primary health care and accelerate universal health coverage in Pakistan, with emphasis on children and women during pregnancy and childbirth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct World Bank press release with program amount, purpose, and target groups; strong for policy design but not proof of rollout.
evidence.period_fit: Published during the 2022 target year and directly relevant to Shehbaz Sharif's premiership.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared attribution: this was a federal health-financing action during Sharif's tenure, but the source does not show a personal PM directive or completed rollout in 2022.
contrary_evidence: Approval alone does not prove full implementation or measurable 2022 outcome.
Health-system delivery remained constrained by preexisting gaps and later flood disruption.

evidence.claim: Pakistan approved a limited national Essential Package of Health Services for immediate district-level implementation at $12.98 per person per year.
evidence.title: Towards sustainable financing for PHC and UHC: The piloting of Essential Package of Health Services in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan approved a limited national Essential Package of Health Services for immediate district-level implementation at $12.98 per person per year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO feature story with a specific national package and implementation cost; reliable for policy design, not independent outcome measurement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared attribution through the Ministry of Health during Sharif's tenure; the page shows a national implementation package but not a PM personally authored reform.
contrary_evidence: The package was limited and depended on broader fiscal space for full implementation.
It documents design rather than demonstrated nationwide delivery in 2022.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said it had already delivered more than $2 million in emergency services and supplies, including drinking water, hygiene kits, medicines, vaccines, therapeutic food for children and pregnant and lactating women, and mosquito nets, as part of the government-led flood response.
evidence.title: UNICEF Geneva Palais briefing note on the impact of the Pakistan floods on children and families and UNICEF's response
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said it had already delivered more than $2 million in emergency services and supplies, including drinking water, hygiene kits, medicines, vaccines, therapeutic food for children and pregnant and lactating women, and mosquito nets, as part of the government-led flood response.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF briefing note with concrete response items, quantities, and timing; strong for humanitarian response documentation.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 flood emergency and target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but real: this is UNICEF's response within a government-led flash appeal, so it supports Sharif-era crisis management but not a personal order for each supply item.
contrary_evidence: This is emergency relief in response to catastrophic damage, not evidence of durable system improvement by itself.
The note also describes severe service disruption and high child vulnerability.

evidence.claim: The project will strengthen Sindh's social protection delivery system and promote maternal and newborn child health through conditional cash transfers, prioritizing poor and vulnerable women and children and directly benefiting 1.3 million mothers and their children.
evidence.title: Factsheet: Strengthening Social Protection Delivery System in Sindh
evidence.excerpt: The project will strengthen Sindh's social protection delivery system and promote maternal and newborn child health through conditional cash transfers, prioritizing poor and vulnerable women and children and directly benefiting 1.3 million mothers and their children.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct World Bank factsheet with explicit target population, mechanism, and delivery-system details.
evidence.period_fit: Published in the target year and directly tied to flood recovery and social protection.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared attribution only: the project fits the Sharif-era federal/provincial recovery environment, but the factsheet does not show personal PM implementation control.
contrary_evidence: The project is province-specific and partner-dependent, so attribution to the federal PM is partial.
The factsheet describes planned benefits and system strengthening rather than measured outcomes by year-end.

evidence.claim: WFP said it was stepping up support to the government relief effort and aimed to reach up to 1 million people with food, nutrition, and livelihoods assistance, including 31,000 children and 28,000 pregnant and breastfeeding women with specialized nutritious foods.
evidence.title: WFP steps up humanitarian support to government relief efforts as Pakistan reels from devastating floods
evidence.excerpt: WFP said it was stepping up support to the government relief effort and aimed to reach up to 1 million people with food, nutrition, and livelihoods assistance, including 31,000 children and 28,000 pregnant and breastfeeding women with specialized nutritious foods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct WFP operational update with concrete beneficiary counts and categories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect and shared: the government was leading the national emergency response, while WFP was the external operational partner.
contrary_evidence: This is humanitarian relief in response to disaster, not evidence of structural welfare reform.
The source shows severe access constraints and worsening humanitarian conditions.

evidence.claim: WHO said the Government of Pakistan had delivered an impressive rescue and first-phase relief operation and that decisive early warning and immediate response actions by the government and local communities helped save lives, while urgent action was still needed to prevent disease and severe acute malnutrition.
evidence.title: WHO Director-General's remarks at the OCHA briefing on the emergency flood response in Pakistan - 4 October 2022
evidence.excerpt: WHO said the Government of Pakistan had delivered an impressive rescue and first-phase relief operation and that decisive early warning and immediate response actions by the government and local communities helped save lives, while urgent action was still needed to prevent disease and severe acute malnutrition.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO leadership remarks, useful for response assessment though still a humanitarian-and-coordination perspective rather than an audit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relatively strong attribution for crisis management because the WHO head explicitly credits government early warning and response, though not every implementation detail is attributable to Sharif personally.
contrary_evidence: WHO also described a looming public health disaster and disrupted health services.
The praise is for emergency response, not for long-run social development.

evidence.claim: WHO said it carried out a measles-rubella vaccination campaign in 38 districts and vaccinated 1.8 million children aged six months to 59 months to help control transmission after the floods.
evidence.title: Impact in 2022 - Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: WHO said it carried out a measles-rubella vaccination campaign in 38 districts and vaccinated 1.8 million children aged six months to 59 months to help control transmission after the floods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO program report with specific campaign scope and beneficiary count.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: the campaign is a WHO response supporting Pakistan's flood-affected health system, not a PM-ordered vaccination directive, but it does reflect the government's crisis environment and cooperation.
contrary_evidence: The same page says about 10% of health facilities were damaged or destroyed and more than eight million people needed urgent health assistance.
This is a remediation response to severe disruption, not a clean baseline success story.

evidence.claim: FAO provided emergency agricultural assistance to 40,000 flood-affected families, targeting communities in Balochistan and Sindh and focusing especially on women-headed households to restore livelihoods and improve food security.
evidence.title: Rebuilding the Livelihoods of Flood-Affected Rural Communities
evidence.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
evidence.excerpt: FAO provided emergency agricultural assistance to 40,000 flood-affected families, targeting communities in Balochistan and Sindh and focusing especially on women-headed households to restore livelihoods and improve food security.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: FAO success story with specific beneficiary counts, geography, and intervention details; publication date is not explicit on the page so the date is marked unknown.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on the 2022 floods and directly relevant to the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect and shared: this is partner-led recovery work in a Sharif-era flood context, not direct PM execution.
contrary_evidence: This is humanitarian livelihood repair after disaster rather than evidence of ordinary-year social progress.
The source is retrospective and does not itself prove federal policy quality.

evidence.claim: After meeting Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, the World Bank said it would provide immediate financing to support social protection for people most affected by flooding and rebuild roads, dams, houses, schools, and health centers damaged by the floods.
evidence.title: Readout from World Bank Group President David Malpass's Meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: After meeting Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, the World Bank said it would provide immediate financing to support social protection for people most affected by flooding and rebuild roads, dams, houses, schools, and health centers damaged by the floods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct World Bank readout of a PM meeting, with concrete financing and reconstruction targets.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 flood emergency and Sharif's term.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the page anchors the commitment in a meeting with Sharif, but the actual financing and implementation belong to the World Bank and broader government system.
contrary_evidence: This is a financing commitment rather than completed reconstruction.
The source reflects flood recovery under severe disaster pressure, not a normal welfare baseline.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif launched the 4RF for Pakistan Floods 2022, describing it as a short-, medium-, and long-term climate-resilient action plan for rehabilitation and reconstruction after the floods.
evidence.title: Prime Minister of Pakistan Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif launches the Resilient, Recovery, Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Framework (4RF) for Pakistan Floods
evidence.publisher: Press Information Department, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif launched the 4RF for Pakistan Floods 2022, describing it as a short-, medium-, and long-term climate-resilient action plan for rehabilitation and reconstruction after the floods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release with explicit PM action and policy framing, but it is self-reporting and not independently audited.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in the target year and tied to the 2022 flood recovery process.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct: the PM is explicitly named as the launcher and the document says he directed dissemination and stakeholder engagement.
contrary_evidence: The release is about framework launch, not verified implementation or welfare outcomes.
It is a government self-report and needs corroboration from later delivery evidence.

evidence.claim: A countrywide consultation produced a maternal nutrition strategy to protect and promote diets, practices, and services for women in Pakistan, with evidence-based and equity-based nutrition programmes focused on pregnancy, breastfeeding, and preventing malnutrition.
evidence.title: Pakistan Maternal Nutrition Strategy 2022-27
evidence.excerpt: A countrywide consultation produced a maternal nutrition strategy to protect and promote diets, practices, and services for women in Pakistan, with evidence-based and equity-based nutrition programmes focused on pregnancy, breastfeeding, and preventing malnutrition.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Joint UNICEF and Government of Pakistan strategy document with clear policy aims and publication date in the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Published in the target year and explicitly spans 2022-27.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shared attribution: the strategy was formulated with the Government of Pakistan, but the page does not show a personal PM directive or a completed national rollout by year-end.
contrary_evidence: A strategy document is not the same as delivered services or improved outcomes in 2022.
The page shows planning and consultation rather than independent implementation results.
